result:
Nothing in the `ces-revisions` package works end to end yet. There's no spec with numbered requirements, so I'm staging this as a new project. Every outcome below is a **candidate from `specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md`**. The three research files are background only: facts, options and costs, not a requirement list. Please confirm, cut or reword the outcomes before I write any roadmap.

The brief's design detail stays out of this list: priors, parameterization, horseshoe, the Dynamax/NumPyro split. That belongs to each stage's own design session.

## Candidate outcomes (unranked)

| # | Outcome (what you get) | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|
| O1 | A real-time vintage panel of national CES all-employees, total nonfarm plus supersectors, SA and NSA. Each month's first, second and third prints, plus the preliminary and final benchmark vintages. | Small data volume: about 24 series (total plus about 11 supersectors, SA and NSA). Fetch time is minutes under ALFRED's published API limit (about 120 requests/min, needs a key). **Vintage depth per series is unknown** until one real fetch. The Oct 2025 shutdown gap (October folded into November's release) needs explicit handling. |
| O2 | Revision magnitude by stage over time: dispersion and tails per stage, per year and regime, for the four stages kept separate. | Cheap once O1 exists: arithmetic on the panel. |
| O3 | An accounting split of SA one- and two-month revisions into an NSA-sample part and a seasonal-factor part, from paired SA/NSA vintages. | Cheap if implied factors (NSA/SA per vintage) are good enough. Unknown if exact factor vintages are needed; the core run tells. |
| O4 | A monthly collection-interval covariate (days from the reference week to first closing and release) plus first-, second- and third-closing collection rates. | Interval: computable from release calendars, low cost. Collection rates: coverage depth unknown until checked against BLS tables. |
| O5 | Annual capacity covariates: real BLS appropriations, FTE, CES sample size, and shutdown/CR/sequestration indicators. Party control is a descriptive label only. | **Mostly your time.** Hand-built from roughly 30+ congressional budget justifications plus FedScope/OPM. Hours to days; I can't estimate tighter without reading the sources. |
| O6 | A fitted multi-vintage state-space model for total nonfarm. It has a latent true path, stage-specific news/noise measurement, and covariates in the log-scale of the revision errors. | Compute **unknown until a real fit**: about 40 years × 12 months × several vintages per month. The core stage measures it. |
| O7 | The benchmark entering as an irregular, higher-precision observation, with wedge-back propagated across intervening months. | Unknown; depends on O6's structure. |
| O8 | Partial pooling of driver effects across supersectors. | Scales O6's cost by about 11 or more; measured after O6. |
| O9 | Structural-change handling for 2003 (confounded bundle), 2020–22, and redesigns. | Unknown; mostly modeling effort. |
| O10 | Validation: posterior predictive checks on revision dispersion, LOO against a constant-variance baseline, pseudo-real-time checks, and MCMC diagnostics. | Pseudo-real-time means many refits, so a multiple of O6's measured fit time. |
| O11 | A written statement of which driver effects are identified, off which variation, and which are not. This covers collection interval (within-year) versus funding, staffing and sample (slow and collinear). | Writing time; depends on O6–O10 results. |

## Proposed tracks

- **A: Revision record (O1, O2, O3). Known progression.** It's a usable product on its own: the descriptive record of how revision scale changed. It also tells the model what to explain.
- **B: Covariates (O4, O5). Known progression.** It's split from A because it uses different sources (calendars, budget documents) and a different cost, mostly your hand-building time. O4 and O5 could be separate tracks if you want the cheap monthly covariate without waiting on the annual hand-build.
- **C: Revision-scale model (O6–O11). Research.** The method and the answer are both open. It commits a core stage only (O6 on real total-nonfarm data, with its measured fit cost); the rest waits in a ranked list until that fit runs. It depends on A's panel and, for covariates, on B.

I'm unsure of O3's kind. If implied factors don't suffice, it becomes research, and I'd move it to its own track. Tell me if you see it that way now.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 (`.python-version`), uv, pytest and ruff.
- From the brief: NumPyro/NUTS, Dynamax, Blackjax if needed, ArviZ, Polars.
  - One cheap check I'd run: that JAX/NumPyro/Dynamax wheels support 3.14. If they don't, it's a project-wide pin decision for you.

## Proposed name

`ces-revisions`, giving `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`. No file by that name exists.

## Optional probe

One real ALFRED fetch of PAYEMS and PAYNSA vintages to firm up O1's coverage note. I'd run it only on your yes, since it needs your API key.

**One request:** rank the outcomes within each track and the tracks among themselves, and confirm or change the tracks, their kinds, and the name.
